REPRESENTATION (src/scms_sim_ref/mock_pipeline/roads.py, 703 lines). The road network is a 2-D, UNDIRECTED, node/edge graph with straight-line segments only; no lanes, no elevation, no turn restrictions, no junction geometry at the network level. Four topologies share one duck-typed interface (nodes / boundary / center / _coord / dist_to_road / random_trip / geometry / node_phase, roads.py:8-14):

- Trip (roads.py:23-99): a routed journey = polyline of (x,y) waypoints + one constant desired speed + optional per-SEGMENT speed caps (`caps` aligned with waypoint pairs, None=uncapped, roads.py:26-39, cap_at roads.py:47-54). Position = linear interpolation along straight segments (at_distance roads.py:56-72); heading = segment azimuth (discontinuous at vertices). next_node (roads.py:79-84) and next_turn bend-angle (roads.py:86-99) feed signal stops and turn-slowdown.
- GridNetwork (roads.py:102-300): w x h Manhattan grid, nodes = integer (i,j) scaled by `block` (default 120 m, run.py:416), 4-neighbour undirected edges. Optional dropout removes only non-spanning-tree edges to stay connected (roads.py:137-157). boundary = perimeter nodes (roads.py:119-120). Signal phase = (i+j)%2 checkerboard (node_phase roads.py:162-170). Opt-in 2-tier speed hierarchy: every arterial_every-th row/column is an arterial at arterial_speed, rest local_speed, 0=uncapped (roads.py:108-114, _edge_cap roads.py:172-181). dist_to_road = analytic distance to grid lines (roads.py:183-191). Timed closures with connectivity guard (set_closures roads.py:201-229). ROUTING = BFS hop count, NOT distance/time (roads.py:242-257). OD: uniform, gravity distance-decay exp(-(hops-min)/scale) (roads.py:259-278), dest_hint (commute-to-centre), boundary origins (roads.py:280-300).
- RingNetwork (roads.py:311-370): n nodes on a circle, cycle edges, routes the shorter arc (roads.py:341-344), single optional whole-ring speed cap (roads.py:315-321), phase = ring-index parity (roads.py:333-339).
- CustomNetwork (roads.py:373-680): arbitrary undirected graph; hard caps MAX_NODES=400 / MAX_EDGES=1600 (roads.py:382-383). Edges [a,b] or [a,b,speed_mps] with speed validated 1-70 m/s (roads.py:405-423); duplicate undirected edges deduped (roads.py:416-424); edges <1 m rejected (roads.py:429-430); must be connected (roads.py:433-445). center = node nearest centroid; boundary = dead-ends + bbox-rim nodes within a 12% margin (roads.py:449-457). Signal phase = deterministic BFS graph 2-colouring (roads.py:481-511). Routing = Dijkstra on edge LENGTH (not time), deterministic tie-break (roads.py:561-585). dist_to_road = exact point-segment distance via spatial-hash cell rings + 200k-entry memo (roads.py:587-618). Timed closures (roads.py:518-545), gravity OD (roads.py:620-636), random_trip attaches per-edge caps (roads.py:638-662), geometry export (roads.py:664-667), stats (roads.py:669-680).
- spider_graph (roads.py:683-703): radial arms + concentric rings generator for CustomNetwork.

OSM IMPORT (src/scms_sim_ref/mock_pipeline/osm.py, 249 lines). Overpass `map?bbox=` raw-XML fetch, sha256-keyed disk cache (osm.py:49, 193-209); 11 hardcoded ~1-2 km^2 city bboxes (osm.py:25-37); arbitrary bbox limited to 0.05 x 0.04 deg (osm.py:223-224). TAGS USED: only `highway` (13 drivable classes with default speeds, motorway 33 m/s ... living_street 5.5, osm.py:40-45) and `maxspeed` (km/h, mph, 'v1; v2' first value, clamped 1-70 m/s, osm.py:52-62). EVERYTHING ELSE IS DROPPED: oneway, lanes, lanes:forward/backward, turn:lanes, junction=roundabout, traffic_signals nodes, stop/give_way, access/service, bridge/tunnel/layer, width, surface, name, traffic_calming, ele; turn-restriction RELATIONS are never parsed (only node/way elements read, osm.py:92-104). Geometry: local equirectangular projection (kx=111320*cos(midlat), ky=110540, osm.py:108-116); ways split at shared/keep nodes (endpoints + nodes used by >=2 ways, osm.py:124-131); each chain RDP-simplified at tol 10 m base, escalating x(1+0.5*attempt) (osm.py:65-82, 118-121, 144-156); EVERY surviving RDP vertex becomes a graph node (curve shape points are promoted to fake 'intersections', osm.py:135-156); coordinates rounded to 0.1 m and merged by rounded key; parallel edges collapsed keeping MAX speed (osm.py:155); node budget max_nodes=380 enforced by progressively dropping minor classes living_street->residential->unclassified->tertiary_link->tertiary (osm.py:47, 118-190); largest connected component only (osm.py:159-183). Output: {nodes:[[x,y]...], edges:[[a,b,speed]...]} JSON consumed via --road custom (osm.py:231-245, run.py:743-762, 1473-1475).

RUN-TIME NETWORK BEHAVIOUR (src/scms_sim_ref/mock_pipeline/run.py, 3436 lines). Network built at run.py:1460-1475 (grid/ring/spider/custom; default road_network='linear' = no network at all, straight infinite lines with sinusoidal lane wander, run.py:650-668). Config: run.py:413-491 (grid_w/h=6, grid_block_m=120, grid_dropout, n_lanes=1, lane_width_m=3.5, traffic_lights=False, light_cycle_s=24, arterial_*, turn_slowdown, lane_changes MOBIL, gap_acceptance, od_model, boundary_origins, n_rsus/rsu_placement/rsu_range_m/rsu_coords). LANES are NOT part of the network: a single global n_lanes applies to every road; a lane is a perpendicular offset lane_off=(idx-(n_lanes-1)/2)*lane_width applied AFTER centerline kinematics (run.py:1600-1611, 2499-2504); with n_lanes=1 opposing streams share the exact centerline; head-on traffic is mutually invisible to IDM (heading-diff >45 deg rejected, run.py:2458). SIGNALS: all-or-nothing (traffic_lights signalizes EVERY node, run.py:2241); fixed-time 2-phase, half cycle per axis, phase offset from the network 2-colouring (run.py:2266-2272); approach axis classified by |cos|>=|sin| of heading (run.py:2466 — degenerate on diagonal streets); stop = virtual stopped leader 2 m before the node point (run.py:2468); no yellow/all-red, no protected turns, no coordination, no actuation. GAP ACCEPTANCE (opt-in, unsignalized only): first-come priority per node, conflict = heading diff 45-135 deg, virtual stop 2 m out (run.py:2414-2479). Turn slowdown = speed cap through bends >= turn_min_angle_deg (run.py:2480-2483). Per-edge speed caps applied as v0 = min(desired, cap_at(s)) (run.py:2485-2488). CLOSURES (close_edge events) affect only NEW-trip routing at spawn; en-route vehicles are never rerouted (run.py:1731-1751). Map-matching detector: dist_to_road with offroad_tol_m=15 (run.py:358, 2260-2264, 2827); linear mode returns 0 (no map). RSUs: static trusted receivers placed at nodes — spread/perimeter/center/corners/all or explicit coords; linear = even spacing (run.py:832-863, 1807-1826). V2X radio is geometry-free w.r.t. the map: default unit-disc range (d<=rr, run.py:2728-2730), opt-in 'logdistance' log-distance path loss + log-normal shadowing (run.py:2690-2739), scalar weather loss and a probabilistic nlos_loss knob (run.py:872, 2684) — no building/terrain occlusion derived from the road network. geometry() dumped to network.json for the GUI only (run.py:2213-2217). CLI: --road/--custom-network/--grid*/--lanes/--traffic-lights etc. (run.py:3192-3229); presets all use synthetic grids (run.py:878-897). NOTE the repo also has a MOSAIC/SUMO layer (scms-sim/, SUMO 1.25.0 + MOSAIC 25.2 at C:/Users/Administrator/tools) which is entirely separate from this pure-Python network model.
gaps: No one-way streets or directed edges anywhere: GridNetwork/RingNetwork/CustomNetwork are all undirected (roads.py:374-424); osm.py drops the oneway tag entirely, so every imported one-way street, dual carriageway, and motorway ramp becomes a two-way road (dual carriageways become two parallel two-way roads).

No lane model in the network: lanes are a single global n_lanes + lane_width for every road (run.py:420-421), realized as a post-hoc perpendicular offset from the centerline (run.py:2499-2504); no per-edge lane counts (OSM lanes/lanes:forward tags dropped), no lane-to-lane connectivity at junctions, no turn lanes, no shoulder/bus lanes; with n_lanes=1 opposing flows occupy the same line and pass through each other (IDM ignores >45-deg heading difference, run.py:2458).

No turn restrictions or U-turn prohibition: OSM restriction relations are never parsed (osm.py reads only node/way elements); routers (BFS roads.py:242, Dijkstra roads.py:561) may take any turn at any node.

Junctions are dimensionless points: no internal geometry, no turning radius, no conflict areas, no per-approach stop lines (hardcoded 2 m before the node, run.py:2468), no roundabout objects; vehicles cross a shared point simultaneously unless gap_acceptance/lights are on.

Geometry is straight segments only, 2-D, no elevation: curves survive only as RDP polylines at >=10 m tolerance (osm.py:85-121) whose shape points are promoted to graph nodes, consuming the 380-node budget and blurring 'intersection' vs 'bend'; no ele/SRTM, no bridge/tunnel/layer, no grade effects on kinematics or radio.

Traffic signals are synthetic and all-or-nothing: traffic_lights signalizes EVERY intersection with a single fixed-time 2-phase plan (24 s cycle default) phased by a graph 2-colouring (run.py:2241, 2266-2272; roads.py:481-511); OSM traffic_signals nodes are dropped, so signal placement never matches the real city; no yellow/all-red clearance, no protected lefts, no offsets/green waves, no actuated or adaptive control; axis classification |cos|>=|sin| (run.py:2466) is wrong on diagonal streets.

Routing realism: GridNetwork routes by BFS hop count (not distance or time, roads.py:242-257); CustomNetwork by length (not travel time, ignoring speed limits, roads.py:561-585); all drivers take the identical deterministic shortest path (no stochastic route choice, no congestion-aware routing); close_edge events divert only new spawns — vehicles already en route drive through 'closed' roads (run.py:1731-1751).

OSM import completeness: only highway-class + maxspeed used; dropped tags include oneway, lanes, turn:lanes, junction=roundabout, traffic_signals, stop/give_way, access, service, bridge/tunnel/layer, width, surface, names; 380-node budget (max_nodes=380, osm.py:85) forces class-dropping escalation, so imported 'cities' are skeletal arterial subgraphs of a ~1-2 km^2 core; parallel-edge collapse keeps the MAX speed (osm.py:155) which can over-speed service alignments.

V2X propagation ignores the built environment: default is a hard unit-disc (run.py:2728-2730); the opt-in log-distance+shadowing model (run.py:2690-2739) is still isotropic and statistical — no building footprints, no LOS/NLOS classification from map geometry, no intersection-corner diffraction, no channel-congestion/CBR/CSMA effects tied to local density beyond scalar packet-loss knobs.

No network-level speed realism beyond caps: grid/ring caps are opt-in and default OFF (uncapped desired speeds 8-18 m/s, run.py:422-423, 443-445); no school/30 zones, no time-of-day limits, no per-class compliance/speeding distribution.

No curb-side or ancillary infrastructure: parking, bus stops, pedestrian crossings, sidewalks/cycleways are absent (VRUs are placed heuristically >15 m off the centerline near nodes, run.py:1672-1681, not on real footways).

Scale ceiling: MAX_NODES=400/MAX_EDGES=1600 (roads.py:382-383) plus the RDP-vertex-as-node design bounds any real-city extract to a toy fraction of a district; a real city core has thousands of junctions.
opportunities: Decouple edge SHAPE from graph topology: carry each edge's full (RDP-lightened) polyline as shape points on the edge instead of promoting curve vertices to nodes. Trip already consumes arbitrary polylines with per-segment caps (roads.py:31-54), so _route() need only expand edge shapes into waypoints — this alone frees most of the 380-node budget for true intersections and preserves curve geometry. Hook: CustomNetwork.__init__ edge parsing (roads.py:405-424) + random_trip waypoint assembly (roads.py:656-662) + osm.py:144-156 (emit chains as shapes, not node splits).

Directed-graph support + oneway import: extend the edge schema to [a,b,speed,{oneway,lanes,...}] or a parallel edge-attr dict; make adj directional (roads.py:426-432), route on the digraph, and parse oneway=yes/-1/reversible and junction=roundabout in osm.py:96-104. Keep it opt-in (undirected default) to preserve the repo's byte-identical-output discipline (every existing feature is gated this way, e.g. run.py:437-482).

Per-edge lane counts and widths: import OSM lanes/lanes:forward/backward/width; store per-edge n_lanes; make lane_off per-edge in car_follow (run.py:2499-2504) and clamp MOBIL targets to the current edge's lane count (run.py:2285-2370). Enables real 1-lane residential vs 3-lane arterial contrast in one map.

Real signal placement + richer control: parse OSM traffic_signals nodes (and highway=stop/give_way) into a per-node control type; signalize only tagged nodes (change _lights gating at run.py:2241 and the per-node check at run.py:2462-2470); add yellow/all-red intervals, per-node cycle/offset (green waves along arterials), and an optional vehicle-actuated mode. gap_acceptance already covers the untagged nodes (run.py:2414-2441).

Turn restrictions: parse OSM relation type=restriction in osm.py and store forbidden (in-edge,node,out-edge) triples; enforce in Dijkstra by expanding the search state to (edge,node) — a standard edge-based router — in roads.py:561-585; also ban U-turns by default.

Time-based, congestion-aware, and heterogeneous routing: switch GridNetwork BFS to the same Dijkstra as CustomNetwork with cost=length/cap (roads.py:242, 561); add optional stochastic route choice (C-logit/path-size over k-shortest paths, seeded from cfg.derive for determinism) and mid-trip rerouting on close_edge events (currently spawn-only, run.py:1731-1751).

Elevation: add optional z to nodes (OSM ele or an SRTM tile sampled at import time, cached like the XML at osm.py:193-209); expose grade per segment to IDM (uphill accel penalty) and to the radio model.

SUMO netconvert bridge (highest-fidelity path): the toolchain already ships SUMO 1.25.0 — run netconvert --osm-files on the SAME cached extract to get a .net.xml with correct one-ways, per-edge lanes, speed limits, junction internal geometry, connections, and tls programs; then either (a) run full-fidelity scenarios through the existing MOSAIC/SUMO layer (scms-sim/), or (b) write a sumolib-based .net.xml -> CustomNetwork importer so the pure-Python simulator inherits netconvert's cleaned topology (lane counts, signals, one-ways as edge attrs) without reimplementing OSM parsing.

Geometry-based NLOS radio: import OSM building footprints (building=* ways, same Overpass extract) as polygons; per-link LOS test (segment-polygon intersection with a spatial hash like roads.py:465-473) to switch between LOS/NLOS path-loss exponents or add per-obstacle attenuation — replacing the scalar nlos_loss probability. Hook: the reception loop's per-link dB math (run.py:2732-2739); the ETSI-style corner-diffraction model (Sommer et al.) fits directly here.

Raise the scale ceiling: with edge-shape decoupling, lift MAX_NODES/MAX_EDGES (roads.py:382-383) toward a few thousand junctions; the Dijkstra, spatial index, dist_to_road memo, and _CF_CELL bucketing (run.py:2240, 2408-2410) are all O(local) already.

Junction realism increments: per-approach stop-line offset derived from the crossing road's half-width (instead of the constant 2 m at run.py:2468/2473), turn-speed from actual curve radius once shapes exist (replacing the bend-angle heuristic at run.py:2480-2483), and node-occupancy (one vehicle in the conflict box) layered on the existing gap_acceptance claims machinery (run.py:2420-2441).

Import-side quality knobs: keep service=driveway out but optionally include 'service' and 'road' classes; parse maxspeed:forward/backward and implicit country defaults (e.g. urban 50 km/h) instead of pure class defaults (osm.py:40-45); mark boundary nodes as real map-edge cut points (ways clipped by the bbox) rather than the bbox-rim heuristic (roads.py:452-457) so OD sources/sinks match true entry roads.
notes: Design constraints that any improvement must respect: (1) strict determinism / byte-identical outputs — every existing realism feature is opt-in and documented as 'OFF by default -> byte-identical' (e.g. run.py:437-482, roads.py:108-114); new network features should follow the same gating so existing corpora and digests reproduce. (2) The simulation must stay offline after import — osm.py fetches once and caches (osm.py:193-209); building/elevation imports should use the same cache pattern. (3) The topology-agnostic interface (nodes/boundary/center/_coord/dist_to_road/random_trip/geometry/node_phase, roads.py:8-14) is the integration seam: run.py touches networks only through it plus set_closures/stats, so directed edges, shapes, per-edge lanes, and per-node signal types can be added inside CustomNetwork without touching Grid/Ring call sites. (4) run.py validation hard-codes the topology list and cross-feature rules at run.py:950-1076 — new network kinds/attrs must be registered there and in the CLI (run.py:3192-3229) and GUI help tables (run.py:1129-1232). (5) The MOSAIC/SUMO layer (scms-sim/) is the already-present high-fidelity alternative; a netconvert-based bridge would let both layers share one OSM source of truth.
